const { subagentId } = await startAsyncSubagent({
    specialization: "DESIGN",
    task: `Build a fully playable 3D voxel Minecraft-clone game called "VoxelCraft" in the React + Vite app at artifacts/voxel-craft/. The app uses @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, three, and simplex-noise (all already installed).

**Product identity:** A browser-based voxel world builder and survival game that feels chunky and satisfying — every block placed or broken should feel weighty and rewarding, with a world that rewards exploration.

**The game must include ALL of the following features:**

## 1. Procedurally Generated World
- Use simplex-noise to generate a realistic terrain with hills, plains, mountains
- Generate a world at least 64x64 blocks wide, with varied heights (y=0 to y=20+)
- Block layers: top is Grass, below is Dirt (2-3 layers), then Stone, then Bedrock at bottom
- Place Trees randomly on grass surface: trunk = Wood blocks (4-6 tall), top = Leaf blocks (3x3x3 cluster)
- Generate Sand near water level, Stone cliffs on mountains
- Place water at a fixed sea level (e.g. y=4)
- Add caves (empty pockets underground)

## 2. Block Types
Define these block types with distinct colors (use MeshLambertMaterial with flat colors — no textures needed):
- GRASS: top green (0x567d46), sides dark green (0x8fbc8f)  
- DIRT: brown (0x8B6914)
- STONE: gray (0x808080)
- SAND: sandy yellow (0xf4d04e)
- WOOD: brown trunk (0x6B4423)
- LEAF: leaf green (0x228B22), semi-transparent (opacity 0.8)
- WATER: blue (0x4169E1), semi-transparent (opacity 0.6)
- BEDROCK: dark gray (0x2d2d2d)
- COAL_ORE: dark gray with black spots (0x4a4a4a)
- IRON_ORE: stone with orange flecks (0x8B7355)
- GLASS: very transparent (0xadd8e6, opacity 0.3)
- PLANKS: light wood (0xDEB887)
- COBBLESTONE: medium gray (0x9e9e9e)
- TNT: red with stripes (0xff4444)

## 3. Game Modes
**Creative Mode:**
- Infinite blocks, no health, can fly (double-tap space to toggle fly mode)
- Access ALL block types in hotbar
- Can place/break any block instantly

**Survival Mode:**
- Player has 20 health points (hearts display)
- Falls deal damage (fall distance > 3 blocks = damage)
- Player has hunger bar (decreases over time, affects health regeneration)
- Breaking blocks takes time (hold click, show break progress overlay on block face)
- Blocks drop as items when broken, player picks them up by walking near them
- Inventory: 9 hotbar slots + 3x9 inventory grid (press E to open)
- Crafting (press E): basic recipes — planks from wood, sticks from planks, torches
- Animals can drop food items when killed

## 4. Player Controls

**Keyboard (Desktop):**
- WASD or Arrow Keys: move
- Space: jump (hold for higher jump)
- Double Space: toggle fly (Creative only)
- Shift: sneak/crouch (slower movement, don't fall off edges)
- Left Click: break block (hold in Survival, instant in Creative)
- Right Click: place block (selected in hotbar)
- Scroll Wheel: cycle hotbar selection
- Keys 1-9: select hotbar slot
- E: open/close inventory
- Escape: pause / release pointer lock
- F: toggle between first-person and third-person camera
- Tab: toggle game mode (Creative/Survival)

**Touch Controls (Mobile):**
- Virtual joystick (bottom-left): movement
- Jump button (bottom-right)
- Look: swipe on right side of screen
- Break button: tap left side
- Place button: tap right side
- Buttons for inventory (E), camera toggle (F)

## 5. Camera Modes
- **First-person**: camera inside player head, crosshair in center
- **Third-person**: camera behind and above player (adjustable distance with mouse wheel in this mode)

## 6. Block Interaction
- Raycasting to determine which block the crosshair/cursor targets
- Highlight the targeted block with a slightly lighter wireframe overlay
- Block placement preview: show a ghost block where it would be placed
- Maximum reach: 5 blocks in Creative, 4 in Survival

## 7. Animals (NPCs)
Include at least 3 animal types that wander the world:
- **Cow**: large brown box (1x1.5x2), wanders randomly, mooing sound concept
- **Pig**: pink box (0.9x0.9x1.5), wanders randomly
- **Sheep**: white box with grey head (1x1.3x1.8), wanders, drops wool
- Animals should:
  - Walk on terrain (apply gravity, land on blocks)
  - Roam randomly (change direction every 3-5 seconds)
  - Have simple walking animation (bob up and down slightly)
  - In Survival: can be "hit" (left-click), take damage, die and drop items
  - Render as simple colored box shapes (no complex models needed)

## 8. HUD (Heads-Up Display)
- **Crosshair** in center of screen (white + symbol)
- **Hotbar**: 9 slots at bottom center, selected slot highlighted with yellow border
- **Health bar**: red hearts (10 hearts = 20 HP) — top left
- **Hunger bar**: drumstick icons — next to health
- **Mode indicator**: "CREATIVE" or "SURVIVAL" badge — top right  
- **Coordinates**: X Y Z display — top left or corner
- **FPS counter**: top right corner
- **Item name tooltip**: shows block name briefly when switching hotbar slots

## 9. Chunk System (Performance)
- Divide the world into 16x16 chunks
- Only render chunks within view distance (3-4 chunks from player)
- Use geometry merging per chunk (merge all block meshes in a chunk into one geometry per material) to reduce draw calls
- Frustum culling for chunks outside camera view
- Only show exposed block faces (not faces touching adjacent solid blocks) — this is critical for performance

## 10. Lighting
- Sun directional light (white, position above and to the side)
- Ambient light (soft blue sky ambient)
- Sky color: day = blue gradient (0x87CEEB at top, lighter at horizon)
- Fog: distance fog for visual depth (fogColor matches sky, fogNear=40, fogFar=80)

## Technical Implementation Notes
- Use React Three Fiber's Canvas component as the full-screen game canvas
- Use @react-three/drei KeyboardControls for keyboard input
- Use useFrame for game loop updates
- Use useRef for mutable game state (not useState) inside the game loop
- Store world blocks in a flat Uint8Array or a Map with "x,y,z" string keys
- Pre-generate all chunks at start, store in a worldRef
- For the merged chunk geometry: use BufferGeometry with manually built positions/normals/uvs arrays
- Animal AI: use useFrame, update position every frame, change direction based on a timer stored in ref
- Pointer lock API for mouse look in first-person
- Touch events for mobile controls
- Do NOT use any physics library — implement simple gravity and AABB collision manually
- Movement: apply velocity, then check and resolve collisions against solid blocks

## Architecture
Split into these files:
- src/game/Game.tsx — main Canvas + scene setup
- src/game/World.tsx — chunk generation, rendering, chunk mesh builder
- src/game/Player.tsx — player movement, collision, camera
- src/game/Animals.tsx — animal NPC logic and rendering
- src/game/HUD.tsx — all HTML overlay UI (hotbar, health, hunger, mode)
- src/game/Inventory.tsx — inventory/crafting UI
- src/game/TouchControls.tsx — touch joystick and buttons
- src/game/worldGen.ts — simplex noise terrain generation
- src/game/blocks.ts — block type definitions, colors, properties
- src/game/usePointerLock.ts — pointer lock hook
- src/App.tsx — just renders <Game /> (replace the boilerplate)
- src/index.css — set body/html to margin:0, overflow:hidden, background:#000

**Important rules:**
- Do not use emojis in the UI — use text labels and SVG/CSS shapes instead
- Dark UI with light text for all HUD elements
- Never use Math.random() directly in JSX render — pre-calculate in useMemo or outside
- Import * as THREE from "three" wherever THREE types are needed
- Only use block face optimization (don't render hidden faces) — this is essential
- The game must not crash on startup — add try/catch around world generation
- Start the player at a safe spawn point above the terrain (find highest block at center of world + 2)
- Make sure pointer lock works: clicking the canvas should lock the pointer for first-person mode
- Show a "Click to Play" overlay before pointer lock is acquired
- Log to console when controls are working (e.g. "WASD registered", "pointer locked")

**App.tsx should look like:**
\`\`\`tsx
import Game from './game/Game';
export default function App() { return <Game />; }
\`\`\`

Do not use emojis anywhere in the UI.`,

---
name: VoxelCraft Inventory Architecture
description: How inventory counts flow between Game.tsx (state) and Player.tsx (useFrame)
---

Player does NOT manage inventory state — Game.tsx owns it via `countsRef` (mutable ref for sync useFrame access) + `uiState.counts` (React state for rendering).

**Why:** Player's useFrame needs synchronous count reads (can't wait for React re-render). Game needs counts for crafting/inventory UI.

**Flow:**
- Player calls `onBlockBreak(type)` / `onBlockPlace(type)` callbacks → Game mutates `countsRef` + queues `setUiState`
- Player calls `canPlace(type)` → reads `countsRef.current` directly (synchronous)
- Crafting modifies `countsRef.current` then calls `setUiState` for new hotbar
- `externalHotbar` prop flows Game→Player; Player syncs via `useEffect` (only fires when ref changes, e.g. after craft)

**How to apply:** Always keep `countsRef.current` and `uiState.counts` in sync — mutate the ref first, then queue the state update.

---
name: Pixel Art Texture Atlas
description: How the 8×8 pixel block texture atlas works in World.tsx
---

Atlas is 128×128px (16 cols × 16 rows, 8px per tile). Block type value = tile index (bt % 16 = col, floor(bt/16) = row).

UV formula: `[col/16, 1-(row+1)/16, 1/16, 1/16]` — note the Y-flip since canvas is top-down but UV is bottom-up.

In World.tsx, vertex colors are set to `(lightFactor, lightFactor, lightFactor)` — grayscale only. The actual block color comes from the texture atlas. MeshLambertMaterial multiplies vertexColors × texture, giving correct face shading on top of pixel art.

**Why:** Separating lighting (vertex) from color (texture) lets the atlas encode any pixel pattern per block without needing per-vertex color baking.

**How to apply:** Always use `magFilter: NearestFilter, minFilter: NearestFilter` on the atlas texture to keep the pixelated look sharp. Atlas is built once and cached in `_atlas` singleton.

---
name: Mobile Touch Fix Patterns
description: How to make UI elements reliably tappable on mobile inside R3F canvas
---

Three layers of protection needed for mobile UI inside a full-screen R3F canvas:

1. **`data-no-look="1"`** on modal root div → TouchControls skips look-handling for touches inside.
2. **`data-touch-btn="1"`** on individual buttons → TouchControls joystick also skips these.
3. **`onTouchStart={e => { e.stopPropagation(); e.preventDefault(); doAction(); }}`** on each interactive element → eliminates 300ms tap delay and prevents canvas from capturing the touch.

**Why:** R3F canvas captures all pointer events. Without onTouchStart+preventDefault, onClick fires after 300ms delay (or not at all) on mobile because the browser treats the touch as a potential scroll/pan gesture first.

**How to apply:** Any overlay modal needs data-no-look on root; any button inside it needs data-touch-btn + onTouchStart handler. Both are required — data-no-look alone doesn't make clicks fast.
